Coverage-standardised beta diversity with Hill numbers

Source: R/beta-hill.R
beta_hill.Rd

Gamma, alpha and beta diversity of order q, standardised to a common sample coverage, following Chao et al. (2023) (the iNEXT.beta3D framework). Each .by group is a region whose sites are its assemblages. Gamma diversity is the diversity of the pooled region; alpha diversity is computed from the species-by-site data and divided by the number of sites; each is rarefied or extrapolated to the sample size at which it reaches the target coverage. Beta = gamma / alpha is the effective number of completely distinct assemblages (1 to N).

Usage

beta_hill(
  data,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  q = c(0, 1, 2),
  coverage = NULL,
  type = c("TD", "PD", "FD"),
  tree = NULL,
  reftime = NULL,
  pd_unit = c("mean", "total"),
  distance = NULL,
  tau = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  n_units = NULL,
  nboot = 0,
  conf = 0.95,
  .by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

q

Orders of diversity.

coverage

Target sample coverage(s) in (0, 1]. By default, the lowest coverage that the pooled data of every region reaches at twice its sample size, so no region is extrapolated too far.

type

Diversity dimension: "TD" (taxonomic, the default), "PD" (phylogenetic, needs tree) or "FD" (functional, needs distance). Give several, such as c("TD", "PD"), or "all" for all three, to analyse the dimensions together: the results are stacked in one tibble with a type column, and autoplot() shows them side by side. All three are Hill numbers of the same order q, in units of effective numbers of species (Chao, Chiu and Jost 2014), and reproduce iNEXT.3D.

tree

For type = "PD", a rooted ape::phylo tree with branch lengths whose tip labels include every species.

reftime

For type = "PD", the reference time (tree depth) at which diversity is measured. Defaults to the age of the root of the tree pruned to the species in data.

pd_unit

For type = "PD", "mean" (the default) divides phylogenetic diversity by reftime, giving the effective number of lineages on the same scale as species; "total" gives effective total branch length.

distance

For type = "FD", a species-by-species distance matrix (or stats::dist object) with names matching the species, scaled to lie between 0 and 1, for example from Gower distances of traits.

tau

For type = "FD", the distance threshold below which species are treated as functionally identical. Defaults to the mean distance between two individuals in the pooled data. Use "auc" to integrate over all thresholds from 0 to 1 (Chao et al. 2019).

unit

For incidence data, the column naming the sampling unit (a trap, bait, plot or survey day) in which each species was detected. Each site is then described by the number of units in which each species was found and the number of units sampled, and every estimate is incidence-based (Chao et al. 2014), for TD, PD and FD alike. Leave NULL for abundance data.

n_units

For incidence data, a column giving the number of units sampled at each site, constant within a site. Use it when some units detected no species and so do not appear in the data. By default the number of distinct units in the data is used.

nboot

Number of bootstrap replicates for confidence intervals; 0 for none.

conf

Confidence level.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping columns, kept in the output. Grouped data frames are also respected.

Value

A tibble with the .by columns, q, coverage, the sample sizes m_gamma and m_alpha, gamma, alpha, beta, n_sites, the four dissimilarities and, with nboot > 0, their confidence limits.

Details

Standardising by coverage removes the dependence of beta diversity on sample size and completeness, so regions sampled with different effort can be compared (Chao et al. 2023). Four normalised dissimilarities in 0-1 are derived from beta:

  • dis_sorensen (1 - C): Sorensen-type non-overlap;

  • dis_jaccard (1 - U): Jaccard-type non-overlap;

  • dis_turnover_sorensen (1 - V): Sorensen-type turnover;

  • dis_turnover_jaccard (1 - S): Jaccard-type turnover.

For q = 0 they reduce to the classic Sorensen and Jaccard family; for q = 1 and 2 they generalise Horn and Morisita-Horn overlap.

Dimensions and data types

type = "PD" gives phylogenetic beta diversity from tree, and type = "FD" functional beta diversity from distance, exactly as in iNEXT.beta3D. Sample sizes are always those at which the taxonomic data reach the target coverage. For FD, tau = "auc" integrates gamma, alpha and beta over 30 thresholds between 0 and 1, as iNEXT.beta3D does.

With unit, the data are incidences: each site was surveyed in the same T sampling units (plots, visits, traps), and a unit's label must identify the same unit at every site of a region, because gamma diversity counts a species as present in a unit if it was found there at any site.

Confidence intervals

With nboot > 0, every region is resampled as a whole (Chao et al. 2023): each site's community, including estimated undetected species, is redrawn with its sample size (or units) and all quantities are recomputed at the same coverage. Each estimate gets _lower and _upper columns, the estimate -/+ z x bootstrap standard error, kept within each quantity's range (beta in 1 to N, dissimilarities in 0 to 1).

References

Chao, A., Thorn, S., Chiu, C.-H. et al. (2023). Rarefaction and extrapolation with beta diversity under a framework of Hill numbers: the iNEXT.beta3D standardization. Ecological Monographs, 93, e1588. doi:10.1002/ecm.1588

Examples

beta_hill(png_ants, .by = season, coverage = 0.9)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 13
#>   season     q coverage m_gamma m_alpha gamma alpha  beta n_sites dis_sorensen
#>   <chr>  <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <int>        <dbl>
#> 1 dry        0      0.9    150.    244.  44.4 14.5   3.06       5        0.516
#> 2 dry        1      0.9    150.    244.  31.0  9.93  3.12       5        0.707
#> 3 dry        2      0.9    150.    244.  23.3  6.97  3.35       5        0.877
#> 4 wet        0      0.9    260.    481.  64.1 23.5   2.73       5        0.431
#> 5 wet        1      0.9    260.    481.  35.4 12.3   2.86       5        0.654
#> 6 wet        2      0.9    260.    481.  21.4  7.08  3.02       5        0.836
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: dis_jaccard <dbl>, dis_turnover_sorensen <dbl>,
#> #   dis_turnover_jaccard <dbl>
